verdict.line: You lose extended auto-for-auto trades before level 6 while Sett's passive regen and Q burst outscale you; you claw it back once Stormbringer lets you pick short, sharp fights instead.

brief.thesis: Sett's kit is built to punish exactly the kind of prolonged melee exchange Volibear's early game relies on — Pit Grit regens him harder the lower his health drops, and Knuckle Down (Q) loads bonus max-health damage onto his next two autos. Standing and trading hit-for-hit with him bleeds HP you don't get back. Volibear has to convert this into a lane of short, deliberate trades punctuated by Sky Splitter (E) rather than a standing brawl, and only commit to full all-ins once Stormbringer (R) is live to give him the HP buffer and slow to actually finish the fight.

theirWindow.what: His next two attacks carry bonus damage based on your max health, on a 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown that gets very short by level 9 — do not trade autos back and forth here; step out of his 25000-range Haymaker isn't the threat, the loaded Q autos are.

yourWindow.when: Sett's E and W are both down
yourWindow.what: Facebreaker (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s CD) and Haymaker (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s CD) are his only answers to being locked down — with both on cooldown, walk in and land W (Frenzied Maul) twice on him for the bonus damage and heal, or open with Q (Thundering Smash) to stun before chaining E (Sky Splitter).

start.why: Measured at 49.2% win rate over 61 games — the lifesteal on-hit helps you win the regen race Sett's passive is built around, which Doran's Ring's mana-focused stats don't address in a lane with no real mana problem.

boots.why: 47.4% win rate over 192 games — Sett is a pure physical auto-attacker whose Q specifically loads his autos, so the flat physical reduction directly undercuts the exact damage source that wins him the early trades.

core.why: Builds toward the attack speed that feeds Frenzied Maul's double-tap heal, letting you sustain through his Q windows instead of just absorbing them.
Cooldown refund on crit keeps your W and E cycling faster, which matters because Sky Splitter is your main tool for threatening him before his Grit shield banks.
Boosts the healing from W's double-tap and your passive on-hit magic damage, directly counteracting Pit Grit's regen advantage in extended skirmishes.

situational.when: sett is still winning extended duels against you even after your core items
the game goes long and you need more raw damage and sustain in skirmishes
you need the active heal and slow to disengage from his repeated all-in attempts
you're already ahead and want to lock the lane down with more tank stats

runes.keystoneWhy: Measured at 50% win rate over this page's sample — every stick with W procs Grasp for bonus max-health damage plus a heal, which is the single best counter to standing in Sett's Pit Grit regen race, and Second Wind heals back the chip damage from his Q-loaded autos.

summoners.why: Exhaust+Flash measures at 56% win rate versus Ignite's 43.3% in this matchup specifically because it directly defuses Sett's Q-loaded autos and his R grab — the two windows where he actually kills you — rather than racing a DOT against a champion whose passive heals him back up.

playing.title: Don't autoattack through Knuckle Down
playing.detail: While Sett's Q is active (9/8/7/6/5s CD) his next two attacks carry bonus max-health damage. Step out of range rather than trading hit-for-hit.

playing.title: Poke with W, commit only when ready
playing.detail: Use Frenzied Maul to mark and walk out; only recast it on the same target for the bonus damage and heal when you're actually committing to the full trade.

playing.title: Hold Q to punish his engage
playing.detail: Thundering Smash stuns the first enemy you attack after the speed gain (12-10s CD by rank, 300 range) — save it to interrupt Sett running at you off Q's move speed buff rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Fire E before his Grit banks
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (16s CD, 1200 range) damages and slows while shielding you if you're caught in the blast — use it early in a trade window, before Haymaker's stored Grit has stacked enough to shield through it.

playing.title: All-in only with R up
playing.detail: Stormbringer (160/135/110s CD) grants bonus health on landing plus a slow — save real all-ins for when it's off cooldown, since without the HP buffer you're trading into his superior sustain with nothing to absorb it.

playing.title: Watch his HP curve, not yours
playing.detail: Pit Grit regens Sett harder the lower he drops, so a Sett at 30% isn't as dead as the number suggests — only commit if you can finish him before that regen ramps up.

playing.title: Don't fear E as a guaranteed stun
playing.detail: Facebreaker (16-10s CD, 490 range) only stuns when enemies are caught on opposite sides of Sett; in a clean 1v1 it just slows you, so don't disengage a winning trade over it unless minions are also caught.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the trade patterns, cooldown timing, and tactical reasoning are my own analysis of the ability kits.
